scores.claim_text: Defense Aerospace was 17% of 2025 revenue, implying material federal defense exposure via prime contractors and direct DoD contracts.
scores.M_value: 1,539 total federal awards; 1,425 DoD awards totaling ~$27M direct obligations; top recipients HOWMET CASTINGS & SERVICES INC and HOWMET GLOBAL FASTENING SYSTEMS INC; descriptions consistent with aerospace/defense fasteners, castings, repair kits, M119 firing platforms
scores.interpretation: Direct DoD obligations of ~$27M are modest vs implied 17% of $8.25B revenue (~$1.4B defense), but this is expected: HWM revenue flows mostly through prime contractors (GE/RTX/Boeing) as sub-tier supplier of engine castings/fasteners. The direct DoD trail (1,425 awards across multiple HWM legal entities) cleanly corroborates that HWM is a real defense aerospace supplier — no contradiction with the 17% claim.

scores.claim_text: HWM claims worldwide patent portfolio of ~1,020 granted patents and ~180 pending as of YE2025.
scores.M_check: uspto_odp.query_assignee for 'Howmet Aerospace' (Mode A) and predecessor 'Arconic' (Mode B)
scores.M_value: Howmet Aerospace: 35 granted patents pre-cutoff (123 total applications); Arconic predecessor: 85 granted patents (546 total applications). Patents cover aerospace fasteners, blind fasteners, wheels, aluminum alloys, etc.
scores.interpretation: USPTO ODP captures US-issued grants only; 120 combined US grants under Howmet+Arconic predecessor is consistent with a worldwide portfolio of ~1,020 (US is typically 10-15% of worldwide patent counts for global industrials). Subject-matter alignment (fasteners, alloys, wheels) confirms claimed business categories. Well above PASS threshold (heuristic 8: n_granted >= 5 with claimed-category hit).

scores.claim_text: HWM operates US principal facilities including Whitehall MI (titanium and superalloy castings) and Cleveland OH (forgings/castings) - heavy industrial sites with EPA-regulated exposure.

scores.interpretation: Both EPA and OSHA registries strongly corroborate the disclosed principal facilities list. Whitehall MI plants visible across both registries as titanium/nickel foundry operations matching the 10-K description. Clean PASS.

scores.interpretation: Mode A debt issuance is independently corroborated. Mode B is the higher-discrimination finding: a $11.3M DISCRETIONARY (non-10b5-1) sale by a top executive landed inside the 14-day window of a Pentagon J-Book release. Per prompt rubric and heuristic: 'Discretionary sales clustered to PB releases, earnings, or large fund-raise dates are SEVE-RED indicators.' Single-event clustering with single-officer drives this from RED to SEVE (n_unique_owners=1, n_discretionary_proximate=1). Pattern is consistent with informed-timing rather than scheduled selling. Worth flagging for downstream short-thesis aggregation.

scores.M_value: 0 hits in Boeing filings under either search term
scores.interpretation: Heuristic 7: zero counterparty disclosure is SEVE only when (a) counterparty large [yes, Boeing], (b) claim material [yes — HWM says Boeing materially impacts financials], (c) revenue exceeds typical sub-tier disclosure thresholds. Treating as MOD: gap exists but is consistent with normal supplier-disclosure norms. Not a RED.
